The operating current, as a proportion of relay rated current, is set by a
 plug bridge and 1x to 2x multiplier. Thus the current setting is continuously
 variable between 1x the lowest tap setting and 2x the highest tap setting,
 eg to achieve of 0.72 x rated current on a relay with plug bridge taps of 0.2
 x, 0.4 x,0.8 x and 1.6 x rated current, select the 0.4 tap and set the
 multiplier potentiometer to 1.8 x
 0.4 x 1.8 = 0.72 rated current

In practice on breaker fail schemes the d.c supply is not applied to the
relay until the main protection has operated.
It is there for necessary to link across the protective relay contacts or across
the appropriate contacts of the trip relay to apply the auxiliary d.c supply to
the relay terminals

items:
Connect test leads between the current terminals on the relay (23-24) and
 the current terminals on the test set this for phase A
Select plug tap to 0.2 and multiplier to 1.0

Inject current and slowly increase the current until the relay operates.
 Note the value of the current and recorded

Decrease the current slowly, note the value of current when the relay
 drops off and record the value of current

Select the plug tap to 1.6 and multiplier to 2.0, repeat the tests and
 noting current values
Repeat tests injecting in B and C Phases

Operate / Reset timing and 
Contact Operation
Operate Time

items:
Inject current at 2 X setting into "A" phase via a double pole
 switch, one pole to initiate a timer on closing
Connect relay output contact to stop timer on closing
Record operating time, operating time to be less than 12 m. sec
Repeat test on B and C phases

Inject current at 2x setting into "A" phase via a double pole
 switch one pole to initiate a timer. on opening
Connect relay output contact to stop timer on opening
Record reset time, this should be less than 12 m. sec
Repeat test on B and C phases

Make a final check that all switches on the relay are set according to the
 setting
Make sure the CT secondary circuits is in normal condition
Return the relay to service
